newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom to build phone lines in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom to build phone lines in Vietnam.

text.p: State-owned France Telecom said on Tuesday it has signed a contract with the Vietnamese telecommunications operator VNPT to build 540,000 telephone lines in a $470 million project over five years.

Under the terms of the business cooperation contract, France Telecom will build the lines over five years in the Ho Chi Minh province, southern Vietnam, and share revenues over 15 years, the French company said in a statement.

France Telecom will also, through its France Cable et Radio (FCR) subsidiary, provide organisational and management assistance and transfer know-how to its Vietnamese partner. The licence for starting operations is expected to be signed shortly by the Vietnamese government, it said.

FAR will provide a technical and financial partnership "to allow VNPT swiftly to meet its ambitious objectives in terms of equipment and service quality," France Telecom said. The expansion programme will double the existing line capacity and includes switching, transmission and cable equipment, it said.

The official Saigon Times daily reported on Tuesday that the state-owned Vietnam Post and Telecommunications Corporation has also struck deals with Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc and Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone to upgrade its network.
Negotiations between VNPT and foreign companies on upgrading Vietnam's primitive telecommunications network have been going on for many years.
